newsitem.title: USA: King's son urges public to press for Ray trial.
newsitem.headline: King's son urges public to press for Ray trial.

text.p: Dexter King, son of slain civil rights leader Martin Luther King Jr., appealed on Sunday to Americans to speak out in favour of a trial of his father's convicted killer, James Earl Ray.

King also urged intervention by those "at the highest level of power," saying a trial of the 68-year-old Ray, who may die within weeks of serious liver disease, was needed to bring closure to his father's assassination 29 years ago.

A judge on Thursday backed new tests on the rifle purportedly used to kill the civil rights leader in 1968, a move that could lead to a trial for Ray -- who confessed to killing King and then denied it.
The decision also pumped fresh energy into the conspiracy speculation that has dogged the tragedy for three decades.

Asked on CNN's "Both Sides with Jesse Jackson" whether he would ask President Clinton or Attorney General Janet Reno for help, King said: "Every possible avenue should be explored. At this point we don't have a lot of time, so I think at the highest level of power there should be some kind of intervention."
King cited the work of South Africa's "Truth Commission" in bringing criminals from the apartheid era to justice.

"I would urge all people of good will and fairminded people to write to the Court of Appeals ... write to the governor of Tennessee, write to the district attorney of Shelby County, insist that there be a trial to bring this out in an expedient manner because we are racing against the clock here," King said.

Because Ray pleaded guilty 11 months after the slaying he avoided a trial and possible death sentence. He was sentenced to 99 years in jail, but changed his story almost immediately and said he was a dupe for a mysterious accomplice who actually did the shooting.
King said his family was pressing for a trial because of Ray's terminal illness and new evidence compiled by Ray's attorney William Pepper, adding he had a "gut feeling" that Ray was innocent.
"We're forced to deal with it for once and for all. Only then can true healing occur and ultimately closure," he said.

Representative Louis Stokes, the Ohio Democrat who headed the congressional investigation into King's death in 1977, told CNN he believed Ray's guilt would be proven once again, but he would support a trial if it would help the King family.
Stokes said his panel's two-year investigation concluded Ray had been part of a conspiracy to kill King, but could not identify the co-conspirators nine years after the slaying.
He said the panel did rule out any involvement in the plot by the FBI after a very thorough investigation.
Stokes said any credible evidence that had come to light since the congressional probe should be given a judicial hearing, but doubted reopening the case would reveal many new facts.
